title: Earlier low-runoff periods gave unstable spatial predictions at 11 south-east Australian gauges
abstract: Earlier 13-year periods had mean runoff losses like those after 1997. We tested whether their spatial patterns predict the 2010-2022 pattern in an area held out from window selection. We reused published model summaries and fixed the cohort at 11 gauges in five 2-degree cells. Historical patterns reduced held-out error by 11.7% against a uniform prediction in the main model, with wide conditional limits. They increased error by 98.5% with a cool-season rain term and by 27.2% with four-year rain memory. The 1997-2009 pattern reduced main error by 67.8%, also with wide limits. Fixed 1959-1971 and 1983-1995 patterns gave negative main skill. Results changed with station rain and target period. Similar regional mean losses did not give a stable spatial analogue. Five cells, shared calibration errors and dependent test errors prevent a claim that the recent state is unique. Code, licensed summary inputs, predictions, an arithmetic audit and a static figure are included.

display.caption: Spatial transfer from historical runoff departures. Conditional intervals are truncated at -3 in the right panel. Five cells limit inference.

citations.reason: Reuse six licensed period model-summary tables and test the spatial transfer of historical mean analogues.
Climate controls and early-versus-late spatial comparison motivate the new test.
